built_ideas.title: Cargo Hold
reasons: Puzzle-fitting is real but shallow single-mechanism filler; no engine-building or lasting depth for 200+ game shelf.
Looks like a plain teal box with faint grid, not a fun kid-friendly cargo game; visually confusing, no colorful pieces.
Looks like a plain box with hard-to-see shapes—no color, characters, or excitement a child gift needs.
Plain teal box lacks visual charm/color contrast; too utilitarian-looking to read as a fun giftable conversation piece.
Plain flat teal box with no color variety, texture, or theming—reads as generic plastic, not display-worthy.
Clever draft-and-pack hook, but only 6 rounds/5 dice yields shallow, filler-weight tension, not real heavy-euro depth.
Solo Tetris-in-a-box, no table talk or interaction between players — dead silent for a loud party crowd.
2-4 player draft-race mechanic loses its core tension solo; no bot rival or solo mode included.
Mechanic is a clever Kanban/Patchwork-Tetris mashup, but production is a plain box lid, not a real placement puzzle showpiece.
Grid too small and shapes too basic to feel like a real optimization puzzle worth mastering.
Cold plastic Tetris-box tech vibe, no warmth or classic charm to trigger nostalgia.
Just a plain teal box with grid dents—no wow components or novel mechanism a KS backer would pledge for.
Just spatial-packing Tetris under a dice-draft wrapper — feels like a re-skin, not genuinely new.
Just a plain teal box and grid tray — no dice, no distinct minis, feels empty and cheap.
Boring green plastic box in a photo — no colorful pieces or grid pop visible, nothing to film or flex.
Fiddly small tabs and tiny molded pieces will snap or vanish fast under cafe wear-and-tear.
Industrial teal plastic box with visible print lines reads utilitarian, not shelf-worthy decor.
No visible tiebreak/first-mover mechanics beyond draft order; feels casual, discard-on-fail adds swingy luck, not tournament-grade.
Derivative Patchwork/Uwe Rosenberg spatial-packing clone with dice reskin; photo shows unfinished tiny prototype, not a real board.
Just a plain teal box with a grid and dice slots—no visual pop or craftsmanship to justify shelf space.
